title: Withheld TESS blocks show model-dependent timing forecasts in six southern binaries
abstract: We test six published light-travel-time orbit cases with earlier ASAS-3 and TESS eclipse times. Each fit excludes one later TESS observing block. The main model allows an outer eccentricity up to 0.6. Circular orbits, eccentricity up to 0.9, a survey offset, archival error scaling and a denser period search test sensitivity. 3 of six main fits predict the latest block better than a quadratic ephemeris. ASAS 063202-6750.7 predicts both tested blocks much better than a quadratic model. Other cases depend on the orbit restrictions, weights or period alias. These results test fitted timing models. They do not confirm or reject the third stars. Selection and eclipse templates use the source study; the tests are retrospective. There are no new observations or calibrated orbit confidence regions. We include original code, aggregate forecast scores, fitted states, input hashes and a recipe that keeps source tables in separate scratch.

display.caption: RMS timing prediction errors for the last two usable TESS blocks. Each test uses earlier times only. Missing bars mark insufficient earlier TESS coverage.
Latest-block prediction errors under six specified model and search choices. Lower values give better predictions.
